bounded_statement: Within the visible files, each authorized source item (a distinct ordered k1,k2 pair) enters ttest_ind, a procedure that treats every observation as independent, multiple times: each pair appears in two identical staged rows and each row contributes a value to both samples, so 12 source items are counted as 48 independent observations (df=46).

counterevidence_considered.description: The task instructs applying the procedure to 'the complete staged row sequence', which could be read as authorizing use of every row as staged; however, the same sentence defines rows sharing a pair as the same source item, so completeness of row intake does not license treating duplicate rows as independent units inside ttest_ind.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: The task authorizes the ordered (k1,k2) pair as the single source item and states that rows sharing a pair originate from the same item.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: Every ordered pair appears in two identical staged rows, e.g., (u01,v01) occupies two consecutive rows with identical values.
evidence.observed_value: 24 rows, 12 distinct (k1,k2) pairs, each duplicated exactly twice

evidence.description: The workflow feeds every staged row, without deduplication, into ttest_ind, which assumes all observations are mutually independent.

source_refs.quoted_text:
staged = rows
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]
result = ttest_ind(left, right)

evidence.description: The reported degrees of freedom equal 46 = 24 + 24 - 2, confirming that all 24 rows (including duplicates) entered each sample and were counted as independent observations.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify by (a) checking whether the workflow deduplicates or aggregates by (k1,k2) before testing — it does not, staged is the raw row list; (b) checking whether the duplicated rows could be distinct measurements from distinct items — the task states rows with the same ordered pair are the same source item, and the rows are byte-identical; (c) checking whether the report might reflect a deduplicated run — df=46 is only consistent with 24 observations per arm, ruling that out. The falsification fails; the issue is demonstrated.

root_cause: The workflow passes the staged rows to ttest_ind verbatim (staged = rows) with no deduplication or aggregation by the task-defined (k1,k2) source item, and it splits within-item paired measurements a and b across the two arms of an independent-samples test, so the same authorized independent unit is entered repeatedly into a procedure whose validity assumes each entry is an independent unit.
